claim_to_prove: verifyDeposit() has no access control modifier, and when snapTimestamp == 0 the require check `(_calcNextBlockTimestamp(depositProcessedSlot) <= snapTimestamp) || snapTimestamp == 0` always passes, allowing any caller to prematurely remove a deposit from depositList before the next verifyBalances cycle, causing totalDepositsWei undercount.

initial_state: snapTimestamp is 0 (snappedBalance.timestamp == 0 — no snapBalances call has been made yet)
A deposit exists in depositList with DepositStatus.PENDING
depositProcessedSlot is any valid slot after deposit.slot

reproduction_steps: Define _calcNextBlockTimestamp as: SLOT_DURATION * slot + BEACON_GENESIS_TIMESTAMP + SLOT_DURATION
Set depositProcessedSlot = 1000000 (well after any deposit slot)
Evaluate the access guard condition: (nextBlockTimestamp <= snapTimestamp) || snapTimestamp == 0
With snapTimestamp=0: (13606824035 <= 0) is false, but (0 == 0) is true => condition passes
Demonstrate that any caller (attacker) satisfies this condition and proceeds to _removeDeposit

Show that if snapTimestamp were set to a real value (e.g., 1606824023) LESS than nextBlockTimestamp, the condition would be: (13606824035 <= 1606824023) || (1606824023 == 0) => false || false => REVERT
Demonstrate that with snapTimestamp=0, attacker bypasses timing protection entirely

assertions.expected_correct_value: false (attacker should be blocked — deposit timing not yet verified against a snapshot)
assertions.why_they_differ: The OR condition `snapTimestamp == 0` was intended as a bootstrap exception but creates a permanent bypass: before any snapBalances() call (snapTimestamp stays 0), ANY caller can call verifyDeposit for ANY depositProcessedSlot, removing the deposit prematurely without access control or timing validation.

assertions.expected_correct_value: false (next block timestamp 13606824035 > snap timestamp 1606824023, so deposit is after snapshot)
assertions.why_they_differ: Once snapTimestamp is set, the guard works correctly. The bug only exists in the snapTimestamp==0 window, which is the pre-snapshot state.

assertions.expected_correct_value: true (only registrator or governor should call verifyDeposit)
assertions.actual_buggy_value: false (function is declared `external` with no modifier — any address can call it)
assertions.why_they_differ: Missing `onlyRegistratorOrGovernor` modifier on the function declaration.

assertions.expected_correct_value: 0 (no deposits should be removed before snapBalances is called by authorized party)
assertions.actual_buggy_value: N (attacker can remove all N pending deposits while snapTimestamp == 0, causing verifyBalances to count 0 in totalDepositsWei for those deposits)
assertions.why_they_differ: No access control + snapTimestamp==0 bypass allows attacker to drain depositList before the verifyBalances cycle, causing underreporting of strategy's pending ETH.

expected_test_outcome: Test PASSES demonstrating the bug: snap_timestamp_guard_passes returns true when snapTimestamp==0 for any depositProcessedSlot, proving any external caller can bypass timing protection. If bug is fixed (access control added or snapTimestamp==0 check removed), test assertions about guard behavior would need updating.
failure_modes: The Solidity source is not directly testable in Rust — pure_arithmetic approach reproduces the logic manually, so any typo in reproducing constants causes wrong results
BEACON_GENESIS_TIMESTAMP or SLOT_DURATION may differ from mainnet values used in the actual contract, causing assertion on exact timestamp values to fail
The bug may already be patched if onlyRegistratorOrGovernor was added after the audit snapshot
The `snapTimestamp == 0` semantic may be intentional as a valid bootstrap state, weakening the severity claim — but the access control absence is still provable
Cargo.toml for standalone pure_arithmetic test needs correct setup without importing the full protocol crate
